_**Agent (2026-07-31 13:42:14Z)**_

We have successfully built the core of DeadReckon’s original promise.

### Successfully implemented

- Durable Jobs with one stable ID, immutable authority, append-only lifecycle history, leases, heartbeat/reclaim, detached supervision and service definitions.
- Explicit bounded outcomes: verified, failed, blocked, cancelled, budget exhausted, needs review and lost containment.
- Single, Graph and Campaign execution through the same Job scheduler. Ordinary runs, orchestration, new chains, stored-plan forks and campaigns now use it.
- Two-key completion:
  1. Contained deterministic checks must pass.
  2. A fresh, independent read-only semantic judge must return `achieved`.
- Semantic `revise` support. Single Jobs can continue within policy; Graph and Campaign Jobs can repair only the merged parent without rerunning successful children.
- HMAC-signed receipts with signing keys outside the agent workspace. Receipts bind the authority, contract, policy, sandbox, source/result revisions, tree digests, gate evidence and semantic judgment.
- Real sandbox-boundary observation. An uncontained run or unresolved `sandbox none` cannot earn a trusted receipt.
- Crash-safe child launching, exact process identity, process-group cancellation, abandoned-child adoption and bounded recovery.
- Campaign sub-plan recovery and cancellation without signalling anything until the entire nested process inventory is validated.
- Isolated repair children that inherit the parent sandbox and remaining budget and cannot fall back to an unowned `sandbox none` run.
- Protection against alternate mutation routes: Job-owned child Runs and nested Plans cannot bypass their parent through resume, extend, merge, apply, steer, docs or export.
- Public foreground `run --in-place` and `run --sandbox none` are now quarantined behind an explicit `--untrusted` capability. Ordinary runs enter durable Jobs.
- A protected operator-capture system outside the workspace:
  - signed history;
  - crash recovery;
  - symlink and size protection;
  - atomic evidence publication;
  - closed envelope parsing;
  - exact deterministic replay;
  - isolated Python execution;
  - receipt and provider-route lineage.
- Transactional verified export with staged output, receipt revalidation, deterministic recovery journals, forced-replacement backup recovery and idempotent lifecycle events.

### Verification successfully completed

- Central DeadReckon binary before the latest hardening: **852/852 tests passed**.
- Operator-capture core: **18/18**.
- Capture helper: **11/11**.
- Python live-trial recorder: **29/29**.

- Codebase integration: **74/74**.
- Verified-export fault tests: **5/5** in the previous complete run.
- Credential-free adversarial matrix: **11 proof groups passed, 0 failed**.
- Real macOS Seatbelt and Docker control-boundary coverage exists.
- Real isolated Graph and Campaign parent-repair tests pass.

### Integrated versus still local

Fifteen Watchkeeper commits are already pushed to `main`, ending at `ad8d12c`. They contain the original Job model, supervisor, semantic judge, gate, receipt, recovery and initial adversarial hardening.

The newest export, capture, sandbox-observation and `--untrusted` work is implemented in the shared checkout but is not committed yet. It is undergoing final regression testing before being divided into scoped commits.

So the durable, independently verified execution kernel has been successfully built. What remains is integration cleanup and proving the promise under real operator and machine failures.

_**Agent (2026-07-31 13:42:14Z)**_

We have successfully built most of the core system promised by this goal. DeadReckon is no longer merely a foreground CLI loop with completion checks bolted on.

What now works:

- Durable jobs: ordinary runs become supervised jobs with IDs, leases, recovery, retries, time/spend bounds and explicit terminal outcomes.
- Interruption recovery: child launch, lease recovery, repair attempts and supervisor state are designed to survive process crashes.
- One scheduler: single runs, graphs and campaigns now use the same durable job machinery.
- Two-key completion: deterministic definition-of-done checks must pass, then an independent semantic judge evaluates whether the work actually satisfies the goal.
- Bounded revision: the judge can request revisions without creating an unlimited loop or fresh budget.
- Trusted isolation: protected gate material is kept outside the agent workspace, and trusted completion fails closed when evidence is missing or suspect.
- Tamper-resistant receipts: completion evidence is bound to the goal, contract, policy, source/result revisions and judge output.
- Transactional export: publishing verified results is crash-safe, detects unexpected destination changes and restores the previous destination after failures.
- Durable operator evidence: capture history and final evidence envelopes use authenticated, crash-recoverable writes.
- Unsafe execution quarantine: direct foreground or sandbox-free execution now requires an explicit `--untrusted` capability and cannot produce a trusted job receipt.
- Adversarial defenses: tests cover forged evidence, synthetic completion, gate access, sandbox escape routes, interrupted writes and child ownership.
- macOS containment: we diagnosed and fixed strict sandbox verification failing because Apple’s compiler lookup attempted to write outside the sandbox.

Integration status:

- 15 substantial Watchkeeper commits are already on `main` and pushed to `origin/main`.
- Those commits contain roughly 56,000 added lines across 144 files.
- A further hardening set—about 10,000 added lines across 61 tracked files—is currently present locally but not yet committed or pushed.

Verification status:

- Formatting, workspace compilation and the focused capture/export/quarantine suites are passing.
- The broad workspace run reached a newly exposed macOS sandbox/compiler issue. That has been fixed, but its final regression run is still underway.
- We therefore do not yet have a completely green final workspace result for the latest uncommitted batch.

What is not yet achieved:

- The full 24-scenario live dogfood matrix has not been completed: 2 attempted, 22 not run, and currently 0 independently verified live trials.
- We have not yet proven real provider execution through worker death, supervisor death, machine restart, network loss and deliberate gate tampering.
- Some older mutation commands still bypass the clean job-oriented product model and need either migration or explicit quarantine.
- The latest hardening work still needs documentation, clean commits and final operator acceptance testing.

The honest summary is:

> We have built the durable, isolated, two-key verified execution architecture. We have not yet accumulated enough live operational evidence to claim the entire product promise is proven.

So this goal run has delivered the difficult engineering foundation. The remaining work is mainly consolidation, full regression validation and destructive real-world dogfooding—not another architectural rewrite.

We have successfully built most of the core system promised by this goal. We have not yet completed the live, real-world proof that lets us call the entire goal finished.

### What is working

| Original objective | Achievement |
|---|---|
| Durable goal executor | Jobs are saved before work begins, receive an ID, detach, use fenced ownership, reclaim abandoned work, enforce bounded attempts/time/spend, and record explicit terminal reasons. |
| Semantic second key | Deterministic checks must pass first. A separate read-only semantic judge must then return `achieved`; `revise`, `uncertain`, unavailable, and malformed results cannot silently pass. |
| Tamper-resistant gate | Gate secrets are kept outside the working area. Markers and receipts use HMAC-SHA-256 and bind the contract, policy, revisions, semantic judgment, containment backend, and exact result tree. |
| One Job model | Ordinary runs, guided review/full-plan work, direct orchestration, stored-plan forks, supported chains, and campaigns now enter the same durable scheduler. |
| Recovery | We implemented lease expiry/reclaim, process identity checks, crash-atomic child launch, candidate recovery, and bounded Graph/Campaign parent repair. |
| Operator surface | `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list`, `finish`, and supervisor service commands exist. `finish` refuses delivery without a valid receipt. |
| Evidence | Jobs leave append-only history, state projections, deterministic evidence, semantic judgments, receipts, logs, and operator-facing documentation. |

Sixteen Watchkeeper commits are already pushed and integrated into `main` and `origin/main`, ending at `ad8d12c`.

_**Agent (2026-07-31 13:42:14Z)**_

We have successfully built most of the intended DeadReckon execution model. The remaining work is mainly integration, evidence refresh, and real-world fault testing—not inventing the core architecture.

What is working:

- One durable Job model now underpins guided `start`, ordinary `run`, orchestration, stored-plan forks, supported chains, and campaigns.
- Jobs are persisted before work starts, receive one stable ID, detach to a supervisor, and can be inspected through `attach`, `status`, `list`, `report`, and `finish`.
- The supervisor uses fenced leases, renews them, reclaims abandoned work, avoids duplicate child launches, and preserves explicit retry, wall-time, spend, cancellation, failure, and review outcomes.
- Completion requires both deterministic checks and an independent read-only semantic judge. Failed checks cannot be overruled; uncertainty or judge failure becomes `NEEDS_REVIEW`.
- HMAC-SHA-256 receipts bind the approved contract, policy, source and result identity, gate evidence, semantic judgment, and actual sandbox backend.
- Signing material and Job control paths are kept outside the worker’s writable workspace.
- Promotion and `finish` validate the receipt and exact result identity before delivering anything.
- Graph and Campaign results are verified at the parent level. Campaign roll-ups are reconstructed and checked, and semantic repair has bounded, recoverable, tamper-checked lineage.
- Launchd and systemd supervisor-service support exists, although actual reboot recovery remains a live-test claim.
- A dogfood framework now exists with 24 tasks, an adversarial runner, operator acceptance instructions, and a passive fault-trial recorder.

The latest working-tree tranche adds further successful hardening:

- `extend` now queues a durable child Job and binds it to the parent’s verified receipt and promoted source tree.
- Parent-state, receipt, or source-tree tampering stops an extension before child evidence is created.
- Public legacy `resume`, `merge`, and Campaign repair routes refuse unowned mutation before touching artifacts.
- `orchestrate --preview` is now genuinely read-only and does not create plans, Jobs, accounting records, or workspaces.
- Operator-capture and sandbox-boundary evidence structures have been added.
- Focused tests for these changes pass.

Integration status:

- Sixteen Watchkeeper commits are already pushed to `main` and `origin/main`, ending at `ad8d12c`.
- The most recent hardening is still uncommitted in the shared working tree: approximately 68 tracked product files with about 11,000 additions.
- The broad workspace regression passed all substantive core, CLI, lifecycle, campaign, sandbox, recovery, and receipt suites it reached.
- It currently stops on two dogfood evidence-maintenance checks: a stale source digest and a passive-recorder source audit. These are evidence/tooling consistency failures, not failures of the durable executor itself.

What we have not yet proved:

- The checked credential-free matrix currently says 11 passed, 0 failed, and 9 explicitly unproven.
- The live matrix says 2 attempted, 22 not run, and 0 verified.
- We have not yet demonstrated a real machine reboot, live provider worker/supervisor death, host network loss, Linux/bubblewrap completion, a strict public Docker Job, or meaningful cross-provider completion rates.
- Documentation still needs updating for the newly durable `extend` path.
- The uncommitted tranche must be cleaned up, fully regressed, committed, and pushed.

So the honest summary is:

> We have implemented the system that should make the promise true, and automated tests cover most of its safety and recovery mechanics. We have not yet completed the integration and live evidence needed to state that the promise has been proved in normal operator use.

### What we successfully built

- A durable Job model with immutable authority, append-only events, fenced leases, bounded retries, budgets and explicit terminal reasons such as blocked, cancelled, failed and budget-exhausted.
- Detached execution: closing the launching terminal does not stop the Job.
- Recovery of abandoned leases, interrupted child launches and persisted Graph/Campaign plans.
- One supervisory model for ordinary runs, orchestration, new chains, plan forks and campaigns.
- A consistent operator surface around `start`, `attach`, `status`, `list`, `kill` and `finish`.
- Refusal of legacy chain operations that could bypass the trusted Job path. These now stop before altering state, Git or the workspace and offer a durable replacement schedule.
- Two-key completion:
  1. Contained deterministic checks must pass.
  2. A fresh, read-only semantic judge must return `achieved`.
- Deterministic failures cannot be overruled by the semantic judge. `revise` can initiate bounded repair; unavailable or uncertain judging becomes `NEEDS REVIEW`.
- HMAC-SHA-256 markers and receipts binding the approved contract, policy, source revision, result revision, result-tree digest, sandbox result and semantic judgment.
- Protection of signing keys, Job authority, proofs and receipt paths from the delegated agent.
- Crash-atomic process and child ownership, including cancellation and retry of nested gate evaluators.
- Explicit promotion: verified work is not delivered until its receipt and authority have been revalidated.
- Protected operator-capture tooling and an adversarial dogfood suite.
- Documentation reconciled around the as-built Job architecture, including the [current project map](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/MAP-OF-DEADRECKON.md:86) and [operator acceptance procedure](/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/WATCHKEEPER-OPERATOR-ACCEPTANCE.md:188).

- The main CLI suite passes all 870 tests.
- The live-trial collector passes all 29 tests.

### What is not yet successful

The most immediate blocker is strict Docker completion on macOS. DeadReckon currently passes the host’s macOS `dr-gate` executable into a Linux container. Linux correctly refuses that Mach-O binary. We have localized the problem precisely; it is not an unexplained failure.

The trustworthy fix needs to:

- package Linux ARM64 and x86-64 evaluator binaries;
- select the evaluator matching the Docker image platform;
- bind its digest and platform into the Job authority and receipt;
- run Docker from an immutable cached image with no pulling;
- preserve cancellation and cleanup of daemon-owned containers;
- package and sign all helper binaries correctly across release channels.

The real operator matrix also remains incomplete: 22 of 24 live tasks have not been run, and the two attempted live-provider tasks did not reach a receipt. Outstanding trials include supervisor death, worker death, network loss, reboot recovery, cross-provider gate attacks, live semantic repair, Campaign recovery, Linux bubblewrap and the public strict-Docker journey.

So the honest assessment is: **the durable execution and verification system has been built; operational portability and real-world acceptance are the remaining work.** We should not yet claim the full product promise as achieved.

_**Agent (2026-07-31 13:42:14Z)**_

The short version: we have successfully built most of the core DeadReckon/Watchkeeper system. What remains is completing a few boundaries and proving the whole promise under real interruption conditions.

Successfully implemented and verified:

- One durable Job model. `start`, direct runs, orchestration, campaigns, supported chains, forks and follow-ups now converge on durable Jobs with stable IDs.
- Detached supervision. Jobs have fenced leases, retries, cancellation, recovery and explicit terminal outcomes.
- Two-key completion. Deterministic checks must pass, then an independent semantic judge must return an evidence-backed `achieved`. The judge cannot override failed checks.
- Tamper-resistant completion receipts. HMAC-SHA-256 receipts bind the goal, contract, policy, source/result identity, deterministic proof, semantic judgment and actual sandbox.
- Isolated gate execution. Workers cannot access signing keys or mint completion proofs. Gate inputs, lifecycle paths and receipt paths are protected.
- Crash-safe execution. Evaluator and worker identities are persisted so cancellation and recovery can clean up the correct process or Docker container without accidentally touching another Job.
- Parent verification for Graphs and Campaigns. The merged parent result—not merely successful leaves—must pass the deterministic gate and semantic judge.
- Durable semantic repair. A `revise` decision can launch bounded repair work without rerunning already-successful leaves; crash recovery avoids duplicate repair launches.
- Safe result delivery. `finish` validates the receipt and result identity before exporting work, with rollback protection if delivery validation fails.
- Operator lifecycle commands. `attach`, `status`, `list`, `kill`, `finish`, `report`, and supervisor service management operate on the durable Job.
- Dogfood and adversarial infrastructure. We have a 24-task operator matrix, metrics collector, protected evidence recorder and hostile tampering tests.
- Clean automated evidence. The last clean source recorded 13 passing proof groups, 0 failures and 39 successful authoritative commands. Eight real-world claims remained explicitly unproven rather than being falsely presented as passed.
- Full verification passed at the last clean committed source, including the workspace suite and `make verify`.

We have also completed and focused-tested three newer fixes that are not committed yet:

- Cancellation cleanup is idempotent under concurrent record removal and refuses foreign or swapped Docker execution records.
- Live evidence now derives the source revision from immutable Job authority and verifies that the selected trial matches the Job’s actual shape.
- Central Job creation now rejects invalid zero, negative or non-finite spend, wall-time and retry limits before persisting anything.

What is currently underway, so I am not counting it as successfully finished:

- Public `--deadline` support across every durable creation route.
- Authenticated “expected negative outcome” evidence, such as proving that a network-loss trial correctly ended `blocked` or `budget_exhausted` without pretending the Job was verified.
- Supervisor-service preflight on the main `start` path.
- Authoritative network-loss and Campaign-recovery trials.
- The real 24-task provider matrix, Linux/bubblewrap run and machine-reboot drill.
- A fresh full-suite run and clean evidence regeneration after the current edits.

Repository state: the goal spans 24 commits. The newest 9 commits are on local `main` but have not been pushed to `origin/main`; the deadline and negative-outcome work is still uncommitted.

So the honest assessment is: the durable execution and verification engine now exists and has substantial automated proof. We have not yet earned the complete claim that it survives every promised real-world interruption unattended. That last portion is now mostly integration, operator-boundary work and live fault validation—not invention of the core architecture.
